tasks.title: Python *args → slice
tasks.statement: Python: def total(*args): return sum(args). Write total(v: &[i64]) -> i64, which accepts any number of values through a slice.
tasks.hint: v.iter().sum() is the sum of the elements.

tasks.title: Default value
tasks.statement: Python: def hi(name="world"): return f"Hello, {name}!". Write hi(name: Option<&str>) -> String, substituting «world» for None.

tasks.title: divmod like in Python
tasks.statement: Python: divmod(-7, 2) == (-4, 1). Write py_divmod(a: i32, b: i32) -> (i32, i32) with the Python quotient (rounded down) and remainder (sign of the divisor), b ≠ 0.
tasks.hint: If the remainder is nonzero and its sign differs from the sign of the divisor, shift the quotient down.

tasks.title: Comparison chain
tasks.statement: Python: lo < x < hi. Write strictly_between(x: i32, lo: i32, hi: i32) -> bool — x strictly between lo and hi.

tasks.title: elif → else if
tasks.statement: Python: if/elif for temperature categories. Write category(t: i32) -> &'static str: «frost» for t < 0, «cold» for t < 10, «warm» for t < 25, otherwise «hot».
tasks.hint: The if / else if / else chain is a single expression.

tasks.title: match instead of an if chain
tasks.statement: Write grade(score: u32) -> char using match with ranges: 90..=100 → 'A', 80..=89 → 'B', 70..=79 → 'C', 60..=69 → 'D', otherwise 'F'.

tasks.title: FizzBuzz with match
tasks.statement: Write fizz(n: u32) -> String: «FizzBuzz» / «Fizz» / «Buzz» / the number. Use match on the tuple (n % 3, n % 5).

tasks.title: Passing a function
tasks.statement: Python: def apply(f, x): return f(x). Write apply(f: fn(i32) -> i32, x: i32) -> i32.
tasks.hint: The parameter f is called like an ordinary function: f(x).

tasks.title: Apply twice
tasks.statement: Write apply_twice(f, x): apply the function f to x two times. Declare the parameter f as impl Fn(i32) -> i32.
tasks.hint: f(f(x)); a closure can capture k.

tasks.title: Function composition
tasks.statement: Python: lambda x: f(g(x)). Write compose(f, g, x) = f(g(x)) for f, g: impl Fn(i32) -> i32.

tasks.title: any
tasks.statement: Python: any(x < 0 for x in v). Write has_negative(v: &[i32]) -> bool using iter().any.

tasks.title: all
tasks.statement: Python: all(x > 0 for x in v). Write all_positive(v: &[i32]) -> bool (true for an empty slice).
tasks.hint: all on an empty sequence gives true.

tasks.title: list.index without an exception
tasks.statement: Python: v.index(x) raises ValueError if the element is missing. Write index_of(v: &[i32], x: i32) -> Option<usize> using the position method.

tasks.title: zip
tasks.statement: Python: sum(a * b for a, b in zip(xs, ys)). Write dot(xs: &[i32], ys: &[i32]) -> i32 using zip (the length is that of the shorter slice).

tasks.title: List comprehension
tasks.statement: Python: [x * x for x in v if x % 2 == 0]. Write even_squares(v: &[i32]) -> Vec<i32>.

tasks.title: Word lengths
tasks.statement: Python: [len(w) for w in words]. Write lens(words: &[&str]) -> Vec<usize>: the number of characters (not bytes!) in each word.

tasks.title: max with a key
tasks.statement: Python: max(words, key=len). Write longest<'a>(words: &[&'a str]) -> &'a str — the longest word by number of characters (the first one on a tie). The slice is not empty.

tasks.title: sum(map(int, str(n)))
tasks.statement: Python: sum(int(c) for c in str(n)). Write digit_sum(n: u64) -> u32 using n.to_string() and chars().

tasks.title: while True
tasks.statement: Python: while True: … break. Write first_pow2_above(n: u64) -> u64: the smallest power of two strictly greater than n. Use loop and break with a value.
tasks.hint: break p; returns a value from loop.

tasks.title: for–else without else
tasks.statement: Python: for-else for a primality check. Write is_prime(n: u32) -> bool (true for primes, n ≥ 2). For n < 2 — false. Try divisors up to √n.
tasks.hint: An early return false inside the loop; true after the loop.

tasks.title: range with a step
tasks.statement: Python: list(range(start, stop, step)). Write range_step(start: i32, stop: i32, step: usize) -> Vec<i32> (step > 0, stop is not included).

tasks.title: enumerate from one
tasks.statement: Python: for i, line in enumerate(lines, 1): print(f"{i}: {line}"). Write numbered(lines: &[&str]) -> Vec<String> with strings of the form «1: …».
tasks.hint: enumerate gives the index from zero — add 1.

tasks.title: try/except → Result
tasks.statement: Python: int(s) in try/except. Write parse_age(s: &str) -> Result<u8, String>: Ok(age) for integers in 0..=150, otherwise Err("…"): «not a number» if parsing failed, and «out of range» for numbers outside 0..=150.
tasks.hint: match s.parse() with an early return Err(…).

tasks.title: raise → Err
tasks.statement: Python: def sqrt(x): if x < 0: raise ValueError. Write safe_sqrt(x: f64) -> Result<f64, String>: Err("negative") if x < 0, otherwise Ok(√x).

tasks.title: The ? operator
tasks.statement: Write sum_two(a: &str, b: &str) -> Result<i32, std::num::ParseIntError>: parse both strings and return the sum. Use the ? operator instead of match.
tasks.hint: let x: i32 = a.trim().parse()?; on an error the function returns Err immediately.

tasks.title: Option from a search
tasks.statement: Python: next((x for x in v if x % 2 == 0), None). Write first_even(v: &[i32]) -> Option<i32>.

tasks.title: Password check
tasks.statement: Write is_valid(s: &str) -> bool: at least 8 characters long, with at least one digit and at least one uppercase letter. Use early returns.
tasks.hint: Three checks: length, digit, uppercase letter.

tasks.title: Clamp them all
tasks.statement: Python: [max(lo, min(hi, x)) for x in v]. Write clamp_all(v: &[i32], lo: i32, hi: i32) -> Vec<i32>.

tasks.title: A builder instead of kwargs
tasks.statement: Python: def window(width=800, height=600, title="window"). Implement the struct Config { width: u32, height: u32, title: String } with a function default() (800, 600, «window») and the builder methods with_width(mut self, w: u32) -> Config and with_title(mut self, t: &str) -> Config.
tasks.hint: The method takes self by value, changes the field and returns self — the chain can go on.

tasks.title: GCD and LCM
tasks.statement: Write gcd(a: u64, b: u64) -> u64 (Euclid) and lcm(a: u64, b: u64) -> u64 (LCM = a / gcd · b); lcm(0, x) = 0.
tasks.hint: Divide first, multiply after — that way the number will not overflow.
